Root cause confirmed exactly as described in meta.json/discussion.md (public V8 fix commit e194d3a40d8e "[wasm] Fix data race on WasmModuleSignatureStorage"): intro commit b9068d13bb1c replaced the Zone-based `signature_zone` with `WasmModuleSignatureStorage signature_storage`, a mutable field written during wasm instantiation (fast-API-call signature caching) under NativeModule::allocation_mutex_, but read by WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize()/EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() (called from NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption(), reachable via GC sampling and the %EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() test intrinsic) without that lock. Because the new storage class keeps its data in a std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>> whose backing array is reallocated (and the old array freed) as it grows, the lock-free reader can dereference memory that a concurrent, lock-holding writer is in the middle of freeing -- a real, ASan-catchable heap-use-after-free, not just a benign/unobservable race. This reproduced reliably under a stress PoC designed specifically to maximize the overlap window (many imports per instantiate to force repeated reallocations; many racing writer/reader Workers; the cheap %EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() intrinsic for high-frequency lock-free reads). pre_intro has an analogous, textually-acknowledged-but-weaker race on the old Zone-based signature_zone (the fix commit's own message: "The same race existed before on the signature_zone_, but looks like it was less likely to trigger") -- Zone allocation is append-only/non-relocating, so it does not produce the same reallocation-induced UAF, consistent with pre_intro running clean across repeated identical-reproducer runs. post_benign restores the missing lock exactly where the root cause says it belongs (verified by diffing wasm-code-manager.cc across all three revisions) and also ran clean across repeated runs. This satisfies the invariance requirement: identical PoC/command reproduces the sanitizer report only in post_intro, and is clean in both pre_intro and post_benign.

agent_oracle.description: /poc/poc.js (run via /poc/run.sh with d8 flags --turbo-fast-api-calls --expose-fast-api --no-liftoff --wasm-fast-api --wasm-lazy-compilation --no-wasm-native-module-cache --expose-gc --dump-counters --allow-natives-syntax) spawns many "writer" Workers that race to instantiate a freshly-built WebAssembly.Module with thousands of imports bound to a V8 fast-API-callable C++ function (d8.test.FastCAPI().is_fast_c_api_object). Each import forces a signature_storage.Allocate() call during instantiation (locked via NativeModule::allocation_mutex_), repeatedly growing/reallocating the module's WasmModuleSignatureStorage backing vector-of-vectors. Concurrently, many "reader" Workers hammer the test-only intrinsic %EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() (wasm::GetWasmEngine()->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption(), which walks every live NativeModule and calls NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() on each) in a tight time-bounded loop. Rounds repeat (building a fresh module and GC'ing stale ones) to maximize the chance that a writer's vector reallocation overlaps with a reader's lock-free read.
agent_oracle.target_evidence:
post_intro (b9068d13bb1c) reproducibly (2/2 explicit attempts plus earlier manual runs) aborts with: "AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... READ of size 8 ... thread Tn (WorkerThread)" with stack:
  #0 capacity gen/third_party/libc++/.../vector.h:396
  #1 TotalReservedSize src/wasm/wasm-module.h:742
  #2 WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize() src/wasm/wasm-module.cc:733
  #3 WasmModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() src/wasm/wasm-module.cc:813
  #4 NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() src/wasm/wasm-code-manager.cc:2908
  #5 WasmEngine::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() src/wasm/wasm-engine.cc:2057
  #6 Runtime_EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption src/runtime/runtime-test-wasm.cc:1041
This is exactly the unlocked read site the fix commit (e194d3a40d8e) moves the NativeModule::allocation_mutex_ lock in front of; source inspection confirms post_intro/pre_intro call module_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() (wasm-code-manager.cc:2908) BEFORE acquiring allocation_mutex_ (the lock guard appears later, around line 2938, only covering debug_info/code iteration), whereas post_benign wraps the whole body (including this call) in `std::optional<base::RecursiveMutexGuard> lock(&allocation_mutex_);` right at line 2908-2911, with an explicit comment "The WasmModule::signature_storage is protected by the NativeModule::allocation_mutex_." A second crash variant was also observed with the faulting READ inside a writer's own Allocate_more_storage()/push_back() path (src/wasm/wasm-module.h:754), i.e. the same storage_ vector being concurrently freed/reallocated while another thread accesses it — both are manifestations of the same unsynchronized access to WasmModuleSignatureStorage::storage_. Under the identical reproducer, pre_intro (1973b12d6241) ran clean 3/3 times and post_benign ran clean 3/3 times (no sanitizer report, normal exit 0).
